name: JMESPath-based JSON subtree extraction
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; exactly ONE runtime read_jmespath call per input, no fan-out over destination types):
1. Split the input into a control byte, a path string and a JSON buffer (e.g. path up to the first NUL, the rest is the buffer). Build glz::jmespath_expression expression{path} (runs tokenize_full_jmespath).
2. Destination chosen by one control bit: glz::generic (default; schemaless value, generic_fwd.hpp:551 — the located node of ANY JSON type is parsed by the full JSON reader: json/read.hpp generic/variant paths, ordered_small_map objects, util/parse.hpp, glaze_fast_float numbers, json/skip.hpp) or the reflected fixture struct Home{Family{Person father, mother; std::vector<Person> children}; std::string address} with Person{first_name, last_name, uint16_t age} (tests/jmespath/jmespath.cpp:11-30).
3. Options chosen by another control bit: glz::opts{} (null_terminated = true) or glz::opts{.null_terminated = false} passed as read_jmespath<Opts>(expression, value, buffer) (jmespath.hpp:994-997). null_terminated=false compiles a different reader with explicit end checks (jmespath.hpp:466-468, 571, 639-641 and the JSON reader); the project's own tests use it (tests/jmespath/jmespath.cpp:360, 372, 382, 434, 449, 463). Both previous LG harnesses dropped it.
4. Buffer kind chosen by a third control bit: mutable std::string (padded SWAR path, jmespath.hpp:824-831) or const std::string& (unpadded).
5. On success glz::write_json(value, out); on error glz::format_error(ec, buffer).
ADDITIONS on top (spare control bits, at most one extra call per input, after the main call): the compile-time read_jmespath<"literal">(value, buffer) overload with a fixed literal path; std::vector<int> / std::tuple<...> / double destinations that select the three handle_slice overloads. The previous LG harness ran 6 destination types + 1 compile-time path on every input and lost the generic/null_terminated=false code (-8 points).
Known library crash on this path (both old harnesses hit it): from<JSON,std::string> 8-byte memcpy past the end in include/glaze/json/read.hpp:926 when a string is read near the end of the buffer.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
glz::read_jmespath lets a caller pull a single value out of a raw JSON buffer by walking a JMESPath-like dotted/bracketed path (e.g. "family.father.first_name", "[2:5:-1]", "a[0].b") without fully parsing the surrounding document: the path (untrusted or attacker-influenced) is tokenized at compile-time or run-time, then each token drives a hand-rolled scanner that walks the raw JSON bytes (skipping object members, indexing/slicing arrays, following nested brackets) until it reaches the target node, which is finally parsed into the destination type. Because both the path syntax and the JSON buffer are attacker-controllable, the tokenizer, slice/index bound handling, and the byte-level object/array skippers are the security-relevant surface (integer overflow/underflow in index and slice bounds, off-by-one bracket/quote matching, buffer-end checks when the input is not null terminated).
- read_jmespath<Path, Options>(value, buffer): target; compile-time string_literal path, tokenized via jmespath::tokenize_as_array/tokenize_full_jmespath at compile time, then walks the buffer through detail::seek_array_index, detail::handle_slice, and skip_value::op/parse<JSON>::op.
- read_jmespath(path_string_view, value, buffer): variant; the same feature but with a run-time string path, tokenized at run-time via jmespath::tokenize_full_jmespath (implicitly constructs a jmespath_expression) and then the same per-token core loop (object-key scan, seek_array_index, handle_slice) — this is the natural fuzzing entry since the path itself becomes fully fuzzer-controlled input alongside the buffer.
- read_jmespath(jmespath_expression, value, buffer): variant; takes a pre-tokenized/precompiled path (jmespath_expression constructor runs jmespath::tokenize_full_jmespath) and reuses the identical core traversal (seek_array_index/handle_slice/object-key loop) at run time, letting the harness separate "bad path syntax" tokenization errors from "bad JSON content" traversal errors.
- jmespath_expression(std::string_view) / jmespath_expression(const char(&)[N]): source/config; constructs the compiled-path object consumed by the jmespath_expression overload, running the tokenizer (jmespath::tokenize_full_jmespath) over the fuzzed path string and recording tokenization_error plus the token list that the core traversal consumes.
Input space to vary: the JSON buffer content/size (objects, arrays, nesting, with/without trailing padding so the null_terminated/SWAR path toggles), and the path string's token forms — plain object keys ("a.b.c"), single array index with positive/negative values ("[0]", "[-1]", huge literals like "[9999999999]"), slices with 0-3 colon-separated bounds and sign/step combinations ("[::-1]", "[2::-1]", "[0:5]", "[5:0:0]" zero-step), chained bracket access ("[1][2]"), malformed delimiters ("a..b", unbalanced "[", "]", unterminated quotes) that should surface as tokenization_error (unbalanced_brackets/parentheses, unclosed_string, invalid_escape_sequence, unexpected_delimiter) versus run-time ctx.error values (parse_error, array_element_not_found, key_not_found, unexpected_end, syntax_error) from the traversal core, plus the Options template parameter selecting padded-buffer handling (resizable vs fixed/const Buffer types).
